title: Open images of representable etale morphisms of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $E,F$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For an algebraic space $Z$, let $|Z|$ be its field-valued point classes: maps $\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$ for fields $K$, identified when they agree over a common field extension. Give $|Z|$ the topology in which a subset is open if its inverse image in an etale scheme atlas is open. An open subspace is a subfunctor whose inclusion is representable by open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion]. Open subspaces of $F$ correspond bijectively, preserving inclusion, to open subsets of $|F|$. Let $q:E\to F$ be representable etale [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its point image is open and corresponds to an open subspace $I\subseteq F$; $q$ factors through $I$, and $E\to I$ is representable surjective etale. For every morphism of algebraic spaces $g:G\to F$, the image open subspace of $E\times_FG\to G$ is $I\times_FG$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. If $|E|$ is quasi-compact (every open covering has a finite subcover), then $|I|$ is quasi-compact. For any algebraic space $Z$, $|Z|$ is quasi-compact if and only if $Z$ admits a surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme.

proof.text: For points_atlas_isOpen_iff, use lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover to obtain a topology tau that is coinduced by the given surjective etale atlas and makes every scheme-source point map continuous. An open set for the final topology of def-a1-space-point-topology pulls back openly along this atlas. Conversely, an atlas-open set is tau-open, so its inverse image along every etale scheme-source map is open; the supremum/coinduced topology criterion makes it open in the final topology.

source.place: 03BX (lemma-topology-points): comparison of atlas and final topologies.

proof.text: For openSubspace_points_orderIso, lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus makes every open-subspace point image open and reflects its subfunctor order. Choose a scheme atlas using def-trf-algebraic-space; test its representable etaleness against itself to obtain a scheme representing its self-fibre product. For any open subset apply lem-a1-space-invariant-open-quotient. Its image subfunctor has the same point image as the quotient map: at a field-valued test, membership in the sectionwise range supplies a preimage representative. This gives surjectivity of the order embedding, hence the required order isomorphism.

source.place: 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces): the image map and its inverse.

proof.text: For etale_open_image, lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus makes the point map open. Its range equals pointImage by quotient induction on field-valued representatives. Apply the preceding order isomorphism to this open range, obtaining A. Apply lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests to the equality of point images to obtain the factor qI and its representable etaleness and surjectivity. The preimage and pullback-image clauses give both assertions for every arbitrary base change.

source.place: 03IR, 03IE, 06NF, 03H4: image, open factor and arbitrary base change.

proof.text: For compactness of the image, the open-subspace point map is an open embedding by lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus. Its composite with the factor point map is the original continuous point map, by quotient induction and the factorization equality. The embedding criterion therefore makes the factor continuous. Equality of image ranges and injectivity of the embedding make it surjective. Mathlib Function.Surjective.compactSpace sends compactness of the source to compactness of the open image.

For points_compactSpace_iff, use lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover to obtain a scheme atlas presented as a coproduct of affine schemes. Compare its colimit cocone with the canonical scheme coproduct using Mathlib colimit uniqueness. Its component maps are open immersions with pairwise disjoint affine open ranges covering the atlas; these facts follow from Mathlib sigmaOpenCover, disjoint_opensRange_sigmaι and isAffineOpen_opensRange. Apply lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas to select a compact open restriction with surjective etale atlas map. Conversely its compactSpace_points_of_scheme_atlas clause gives compactness from any compact scheme atlas. The coproduct and finite-subatlas statements include the empty-index and empty-space cases.

lean.statement: theorem etale_open_image {S : Scheme.{u}} (E F : AlgebraicSpace S) (q : E ⟶ F) (hq : IsEtale q.hom.hom) : IsOpen (pointImage q.hom.hom) ∧ ∃ A : OpenSubspace F, pointImage q.hom.hom = pointImage A.val.ι ∧ (∃ qI : E.obj.obj ⟶ A.val.toFunctor, qI ≫ A.val.ι = q.hom.hom ∧ IsEtale qI ∧ IsSurjective qI) ∧ (∀ (G : AlgebraicSpace S) (g : G ⟶ F), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) (A.val.preimage g.hom.hom).ι ∧ pointImage (Limits.pullback.snd q.hom g.hom).hom = pointImage (A.val.preimage g.hom.hom).ι) ∧ (CompactSpace (Point E.obj.obj) → CompactSpace (Point A.val.toFunctor))
